Each square is a day, each column a week (Monday at the top). Load per ride: hours × intensity² × 100, where one hour at your FTP is 100 (same calculation as Fitness & form). Climb attempts from rides not in the archive count as time on the climb at 85% of your FTP. Colours: below 50 light, below 100 moderate, below 200 hard, 200 or more very hard.

Send climb workouts as planned training to your intervals.icu calendar; from there they go on to Zwift or Garmin if you have set that up in intervals.icu. You can find your API key in intervals.icu under Settings → Developer Settings. Leave the athlete ID at 0 for your own account. The key is stored encrypted on this phone and is not included in backups.
The API key will be removed from this phone. Workouts on your intervals.icu calendar stay.
Invalid athlete ID: use 0 or something like i12345.
First link intervals.icu with your API key in Settings.

A 20-minute test on your trainer: your FTP is 95 % of your average power over the 20 minutes. Export the test as a workout for MyWhoosh or Zwift, ride it, and after the Strava sync ClimbPro reads the result here. Make sure you are rested and ride the 20 minutes as evenly as possible.
Current FTP: %1$d W. Target for the 20 minutes: %2$d W.
No FTP in your profile yet. The blocks are in percentages; start the 20 minutes easily and then build up.
Build up easily from endurance pace to tempo; get your legs and heart rate going.
5 minutes hard, just above your FTP. This empties your fast reserve, so the test then measures your sustainable power.
Pedal easily and recover before the test.
As hard as you can sustain for 20 minutes. Start slightly below the target, ride evenly and give everything in the last minutes. Turn ERG off.

Zwift: put the file in Documents/Zwift/Workouts. MyWhoosh: put the file somewhere you can open on your trainer PC or tablet (e.g. Drive or mail), log in to the MyWhoosh website and choose upload under Workouts. Ride the test within %1$d days; preferably name the ride \"FTP test\" in Strava.

No FTP test found yet. After riding: sync your Strava rides (Rides → Fetch). A ride counts as a test if it has \"FTP\" in its name, or was ridden within %1$d days after exporting and was a real maximal effort.
